content.text:
I have the complete chain. Here's the trace.

h07.

A browser requesting another user's profile image hits `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar`, which serves the avatar directly out of the `avatar_url` column of the `user` table. The full chain:

```
serveUserAvatar — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168
getUserByUsername — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715
Store.GetUser — store/user.go:148
Store.ListUsers — store/user.go (calls s.driver.ListUsers)
DB.ListUsers — store/db/sqlite/user.go:88
```

Notes:
- The route is registered at `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:124` (`fileGroup.GET("/users/:identifier/avatar", s.serveUserAvatar)`).
- The handler looks the user up by username, then reads the stored image straight from `user.AvatarURL` (a data URI) — decoding it with `parseDataURI` (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:737`) and writing the bytes back with `c.Blob`. No separate blob/attachment fetch is involved; the image lives inline in the user row.
- `Store.ListUsers` (store/user.go) delegates to the driver interface `s.driver.ListUsers`; the SQLite implementation `DB.ListUsers` (store/db/sqlite/user.go:88) builds the `SELECT ... avatar_url ... FROM user WHERE username = ?` query and runs it via `d.db.QueryContext`. (MySQL/Postgres have parallel implementations under `store/db/mysql/user.go` and `store/db/postgres/user.go`.)

The data layer endpoint is the `avatar_url` column of the `user` table.
